title: The LaBarbera family band in Mount Morris
summary: Local newspapers covered the family band; his father got the boys going and his mother learned bass to join.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Yeah. I wanted to tell you that I have been, as a child mostly, through Mount Morris many times. We used to travel from Rochester down to the Southern Tier to visit relatives. And when I saw that, about where you’re from and your brothers, and I wondered if the Mount Morris Shopper, which was the local newspaper, did they ever do a story on your family band?

Yeah, there was quite a — actually the Mount Morris Enterprise was the paper before that. There was two papers. You had the Picket Line Post and the Mount Morris Enterprise had early, really early stuff on us in the 50s. What the Shopper would do is they’d put those little photo sequences in. Like they’d put a picture from the past newspapers that were in town and then a little comment on that. But yes they did one on all of us and my father in that paper you know.
Were your mother and father both on the same page as far as, I don’t know if I can say “raising musicians” but I’m guessing this was not a chore for you.

Well no. I think my mother just went along with the program. She played piano and she was interested in music. My mother was a nurse. My father was the one that really got us going with it. And he started us off really and kind of grooming us as a family band, and then we would go out and play jobs with my father or with a kind of a composite of something that he had put together with the three of us. Then my mother got upset because she was left at home, so she started playing bass, learning how to play bass, and then we went out as a family band and worked as a family band.
